hypothesis: Homogeneous-only TRAIN leaves irrelevant-prefix invariance unconstrained; target-invariant mixed-prefix supervision will stabilize ordinary Attention.
supporting_evidence: TRAIN contains only homogeneous phase-0 batches; fixed-self training fully recovers all target configurations; fixed-uniform broad mixing fails
counterevidence: homogeneous evaluation itself has residual seed differences; no ordinary-Attention data intervention has been run
prediction: mixed-invariance training reaches the all-seed stability gate while the matched homogeneous control does not
minimal_test: 25 percent deterministic mixed-invariance replacement versus histogram-matched homogeneous replacement
negative_control: same steps, aggregate token/target histogram, seed, optimizer, and intervention cadence with homogeneous contexts

hypothesis: Useful past-token supervision, rather than invariance, is required.
supporting_evidence: previous-token fixed Attention is nearly stable
counterevidence: the official objective target is uniquely determined by current token; self-only fixed Attention is fully stable
prediction: target-invariant mixed supervision alone cannot meet the stability gate
minimal_test: run invariance-only intervention without any context-dependent target
negative_control: verify every intervention target equals the fixed successor of its current token

hypothesis: More examples or optimizer steps, not context diversity, explain improvement.
supporting_evidence: the canonical training set has only four repeated batches
counterevidence: all arms use the same 320 updates and eight supervised rows per update

hypothesis: Curriculum order or late forgetting, not the multiset of examples, is necessary.
supporting_evidence: evaluation-only Attention removal fails, so trajectory history matters
prediction: interleaving fails or later homogeneous updates erase a mixed-prefix rescue
minimal_test: only if cycle 1 is mixed or transient, compare at most two preregistered orderings with the same multiset
negative_control: identical schedule hash on deterministic rerun

hypothesis: Seeded V/O initialization and V/O-rest co-adaptation are independent of data and persist after adequate mixed supervision.
supporting_evidence: V/O freeze improves canonical training strongly but incompletely; evaluation-only removal does not rescue
counterevidence: V/O has never been trained with mixed-prefix supervision
prediction: mixed supervision leaves seed spread or only V/O freezing rescues it
minimal_test: ordinary-Attention mixed training first; V/O subdivision only on failure
negative_control: nonzero Q/K/V/O updates and active Attention behavior after data intervention

hypothesis: Broad mixing causes signal dilution or averaging regardless of distractor semantics.
supporting_evidence: fixed-uniform causal mixing fails without learned Q/K
counterevidence: fixed previous mixing is nearly stable; uniform differs in support width and signal magnitude
prediction: mixed supervision does not rescue unless Attention collapses toward self/local positions
minimal_test: aggregate entropy, self/previous/far mass, and Attention output norm after intervention
negative_control: reject any apparent rescue with effectively zero Attention

hypothesis: Optimization, normalization, capacity, or evaluator artifacts create the apparent seed instability.
supporting_evidence: historical TRAIN probe, swap, projection aggregate, and parameter-hash bugs existed
counterevidence: canonical AR evaluator and corrected branch studies reproduce the seed-specific anchors; FFN-zero capacity control fails
prediction: no-op identity, row/target/order checks, finite checks, or independent TF/FR parity fail; alternatively matched control rescues equally
minimal_test: fail-closed measurement audit and deterministic baseline/intervention rerun
negative_control: pinned dataset/case/checkpoint identities and exact intervention-scope hashes
